$comment: Machine-readable registry of the ADJUDICATED cross-engine semantic divergence classes for sparq's differential fuzzing (bead sq-0iqzw). [FABLE-5] Consumed by crates/sparq-bench/src/fuzz.rs (DivergenceAllowlist): a mismatch that falls in a class listed here is SKIPPED-WITH-COUNT (reported in the run summary) instead of failing; any mismatch outside these classes FAILS. Removing an entry re-enables the strict differential for that class. Do NOT widen a class beyond its adjudication: each entry cites the spec clause + the bead where the adjudication was performed. The 'engines' field is provenance (which reference engine's reading diverges from sparq's) — the fuzzer consults every entry regardless, so a reference-engine behaviour change cannot silently re-open an adjudicated class as a false positive.

classes.shape: FILTER(?x = C) / FILTER(?x != C) where ?x and the constant C are literals of DIFFERENT comparison families (numeric vs string vs boolean vs ...)
classes.adjudication: Cross-family literal =/!= is a TYPE ERROR per RDFterm-equal ('produces a type error if the arguments are both literal but are not the same RDF term'), so the FILTER drops the row. sparq implements this (passes 15/15 W3C sparql10/expr-equals evaluation tests). Oxigraph 0.5 leniently resolves cross-family = to FALSE (!= to TRUE) and KEEPS the row. Adjudicated in bead sq-eibog; fuzzer oracle fixed in PR #1631 (engine untouched — sparq was spec-correct).
classes.handling: NOT a blind skip: the comparator re-derives the SPEC-correct count independently of both engines (spec_filter_count in fuzz.rs) and absorbs the mismatch ONLY when sparq equals that spec-derived count; a residual disagreement with the spec-derived count still FAILS.

classes.spec: SPARQL 1.1 §17.4.1.7 (RDFterm-equal) — genuinely ambiguous for non-literal cross-type terms (cf. w3c/sparql-dev#112)
classes.shape: FILTER(?x != <iri>) / FILTER(?x = <iri>) where ?x is bound to a BLANK NODE (or vice versa): one side a bnode, the other an IRI
classes.adjudication: sparq (and Virtuoso, and the SP2Bench published expected results) read two different non-literal terms as = FALSE / != TRUE (identity semantics); QLever reads the cross-type comparison as a TYPE ERROR and drops the row (SP2Bench q08/q12b return empty there). Adjudicated in bead sq-ai2wa (2026-07-07): sparq's reading held correct for the benchmark's expected results; the QLever divergence is timing-disqualifying, not a computation error in either engine. Oxigraph agrees with sparq's reading today, and the sparq-bench generator emits no blank nodes, so this class is currently INERT in the Oxigraph differential — it is encoded so that generator/oracle growth (or an Oxigraph behaviour change) surfaces as an adjudicated skip, not a false positive.
classes.handling: Skip-with-count when the mismatching case's =/!= comparison has a blank node on one side and an IRI on the other; anything else fails.

classes.spec: RDF 1.1 Concepts §3.3 (Literals) — two literals are the SAME RDF term iff their lexical forms, datatype IRIs and language tags are equal; the value space is not the identity
classes.shape: An UPDATE that writes a NON-CANONICAL xsd:integer lexical form ("0105"^^xsd:integer, "+105"^^xsd:integer), in any position including nested inside an RDF-1.2 triple term
classes.adjudication: Lexical form is part of literal term identity, so "0105"^^xsd:integer and "105"^^xsd:integer are DISTINCT RDF terms. sparq preserves the distinction (its dictionary fast-paths only the canonical integer lexicals; a non-canonical one takes the general path and survives). Oxigraph 0.5's storage encoder round-trips a typed numeric literal through its VALUE space, so it returns "105"^^xsd:integer for either input and collapses the two terms into one. That is a representational property of the reference store, not a disagreement about UPDATE evaluation. Adjudicated in bead sq-hodke (2026-07-26) while extending the UPDATE differential's generator past the ground-term subset; sparq's reading is the spec-correct one, so the engine is untouched.
classes.handling: NOT a blind skip, and NOT a widening. The cross-engine dataset compare runs STRICT first; only on failure, and only while this entry is present, is it RETRIED under a value-normalizing projection that canonicalizes xsd:integer lexical forms on BOTH sides (recursively, including inside triple terms). The step is absorbed (and counted in the run summary as adjudicated_steps) only if that retry passes; any residual difference still FAILS with the RAW diff. The one property the retry gives up — the lexical form of xsd:integer literals — is then pinned STRICTLY on the sparq side by update_fuzz.rs's unwritten_integer_lexicals oracle: every xsd:integer lexical in either sparq store must be one the generator actually wrote, and the non-canonical generator arm uses a value range no canonical arm emits, so any canonicalization by sparq produces an unwritten lexical and fails. Removing this entry re-enables the strict compare for the class; the test noncanonical_integer_lexicals_survive_as_distinct_sparq_terms pins Oxigraph's collapsing behaviour, so if Oxigraph stops normalizing it goes red and this entry must be deleted rather than linger as an unearned exemption.
